requirements.requirement: Never store raw card numbers — tokenize through the provider (PCI scope)
requirements.rationale: Touching raw PANs pulls you into full PCI-DSS scope and makes a breach catastrophic. Let the provider hold the card and keep only its token.

requirements.requirement: Authorize resource access by ownership, not just by a valid session
requirements.rationale: A logged-in user changing an id in the URL (IDOR) reaches another user's record unless you check they own it, not merely that they're signed in.

requirements.requirement: Hash passwords with bcrypt or argon2 — never store them reversibly
requirements.rationale: A database leak with plaintext or encrypted-but-reversible passwords hands the attacker every account, plus every place users reused that password.

requirements.requirement: Scope every query by tenant so one customer can never read another's data
requirements.rationale: In a shared database, a missing tenant filter turns any list or detail endpoint into a cross-tenant data leak.

requirements.requirement: Authorize downloads — don't rely on an unguessable URL alone
requirements.rationale: "Secret" URLs leak through referrers, logs, and shared links. Check the requester is allowed to see the file before serving it.

requirements.requirement: Store uploads outside the web root (object storage with signed URLs)
requirements.rationale: Files served straight from a public directory can be executed by the server or enumerated by anyone; object storage with short-lived signed URLs closes both.

requirements.requirement: Validate file type and size on the server, not just in the browser
requirements.rationale: Client checks are trivially bypassed with a direct request. Unbounded size is a cheap denial-of-service; unchecked type lets a script land where images were expected.

requirements.requirement: Handle provider webhooks for async events (disputes, refunds, failed captures)
requirements.rationale: Charges settle, fail, and get disputed after the request returns. With no webhook handler you learn about a chargeback when the money is already gone.

requirements.requirement: Send an idempotency key with every charge so a retry can't double-charge
requirements.rationale: A dropped response or an impatient user's double-click bills the card twice; an idempotency key makes the retry a no-op.

requirements.requirement: Treat the provider as the source of truth for payment state, not the client
requirements.rationale: A client POST saying "paid" can be forged or replayed. Confirm the charge server-side (or via webhook) before granting the paid thing.

requirements.requirement: Validate amount and currency server-side against the order
requirements.rationale: If the amount comes from the request body, a user can pay 1 cent for a $1,000 order. Compute the charge from server-held prices.

requirements.requirement: Make password-reset tokens single-use and short-lived
requirements.rationale: A reset link that never expires or works twice is a permanent backdoor if it leaks from an inbox or a log.

requirements.requirement: Rate-limit login and signup to blunt credential stuffing and brute force
requirements.rationale: Unlimited login attempts let attackers test leaked password lists against your users at machine speed.

requirements.requirement: Set session cookies httpOnly, secure, and sameSite
requirements.rationale: A token readable by JavaScript is stealable via XSS; one sent over http or cross-site is stealable on the wire or via CSRF.

requirements.requirement: Enforce a per-user upload quota and rate limit
requirements.rationale: Without a cap, one user (or one script) fills your storage and your bill.

requirements.requirement: Show clear handling for declined and failed payments
requirements.rationale: Cards get declined constantly. Without a retry path and a plain-language message, the user assumes your app is broken and leaves.

requirements.requirement: Verify email ownership before granting a usable account
requirements.rationale: Without verification, anyone signs up as anyone — enabling impersonation and poisoning your user data and deliverability.

requirements.requirement: Strip EXIF and metadata from uploaded images
requirements.rationale: Photos carry GPS coordinates and device ids; re-serving them as-is quietly publishes where and on what your users took the picture.
